content.text:
The first slice of the run is committed and pushed as `8d3c991`. It lifted no sources to VERIFIED, so it didn't do what T-104 set out to do.

**Not lifted**
- **REF-00997:** the publisher returned a 403 Cloudflare challenge. The Wayback snapshot exists (20200305130405), but every fetch of it came back empty, three attempts in both URL forms. It stays UNVERIFIED, with the attempts in its `verification_note`.
- **REF-01013:** re-retrieved with HTTP 200. It is a third-party transcription of the Ontario code, and the page text I read doesn't show the regulation number O. Reg. 163/24 or the edition.
- **REF-01014, -01016, -01026:** compared against payloads already logged in earlier sessions. Titles and years match what is stored, and I noted that in each source's `verification_note`.
- **Why VERIFIED wasn't set:** `amend-source` can't set `verification_method` or `verification_closure_reason`.

**Corrections to the adjudicator's plan**
- It said four code sources had logged 200 retrievals. That was wrong for three. REF-01013 had none, and REF-01014 and REF-01026 were text extractions with no HTTP status.
- It said the unverified-source gap could be filed against parameter 3. `add-gap` refuses that, because its duplicate check matches on `parameter_id` alone and GAP-321 (about the `ratio` unit) already holds parameter 3.

**Tooling issues recorded:** GAP-383 holds the failed step, the workaround and the proposed tooling change for the missing `amend-source` fields and the duplicate-gap check. I also appended the owner-statement ledger entry to `references/project-standards.md`, using only your typed words and a `SUPERSEDES` line for OD-110's ACTION items 1 and 2 (sequencing only).

The data migration applied and the rebuild passed. `research_batch_dod` fails R1, R9a and R9b because this slice logged no searches. That is expected for a verification-only slice, and it is what the languages and jurisdictions run fixes.

**Next:** parameter 12, searching in `lang_jur_map`'s primary languages for Norwegian, Swedish, Japanese and Chinese first. Each search gets a logged prior expectation before it runs. No PR yet, per rule 9.

entries.description:
Search the web. Returns result blocks with titles and URLs. US-only.

- The current month is (provided in the conversation below) — use this when searching for recent information.
- `allowed_domains` / `blocked_domains` filter results.
- After answering from results, end with a "Sources:" list of the URLs you used as markdown links.

allowed_domains.description: Only include search results from these domains

blocked_domains.description: Never include search results from these domains

mode.description: "standard": the normal web search: quick and cheap; right for straightforward lookups (reference facts, official pages, documentation, well-known people, places and topics) and simple follow-up lookups. "extended": a thorough, fresh search at several times the cost and latency.

Rekommendationen i äldre allmänna råd är flackare, 1:20 luta högst 1:20 mellan minst 2 meter långa vilplan.
- **Vilplan:** Boverket säger att ett vilplan ska vara utformat med hänsyn till användningen. Längden på vilplanet ska minst medge plats för en rullstol som manövreras av hjälpare. Den äldre ALM-texten rekommenderar i stället vilplan på minst 2 meter.

- **Ramps are the hardest task.** One study found ramp ascent was the most difficult task for manual wheelchair users relative to other tasks. A separate ergonomics study found that the ramp and 90° turn proved most challenging due to the wheelchair's 65 kg weight and large turning radius, and it recommended design changes that prioritize weight reduction.
- **Fatigue and injury.** Another source reports that over 70% of manual WCUs experience upper extremity pain and injury. A PulseRide paper argues that manual use provides no assistance and requires maximum user effort, leading to early onset of fatigue and risk of over-exertion.
- **Lived experience.** A qualitative study used thematic analysis of interviews with wheelchair users to empathically understand the lived experience of WCUs, and it treats their input as central to designing future mobility devices. A transport study took an inclusive-design and justice approach to the lived experience of wheelchair pedestrians.
- **Participatory methods.** An arXiv paper on accessible routing used interviews, Participatory Action Research and developed a three-dimensional User-Wheelchair-Environment model of accessibility.
- **Practical ramp points.** One first-person account notes that a ramp of greater than about 25° is really difficult to push a wheelchair up, and a Massey University review notes that building codes set maximum permissible ramp slopes.

I didn't find a source that specifically addresses long ramps with intermediate rest landings. If you need that, a narrower search on rest-interval guidance or participatory studies of ramp fatigue would be the next step.

content.text:
A carry-only batch (it searches nothing and admits nothing; OD-84) may be red on R1, R9a and R9b and on no other rule: say so in its pull request body, and do not move `sessions/LATEST-RESEARCH`.

Never claim a batch is done from your own reading of it. Run the gate the
SessionStart contract names:

```
python3 scripts/audit/research_batch_dod.py --session "$(cat scratchpad/CURRENT)"
python3 scripts/audit/adversarial_pass_audit.py --session "$(cat scratchpad/CURRENT)"
python3 scripts/audit/search_log_completeness.py --session "$(cat scratchpad/CURRENT)"
python3 scripts/audit/refusal_register.py classes --session "$(cat scratchpad/CURRENT)"
```

The second line is RC4 (advisory): it FAILs if this session wrote to any of the 2026-08-19
RULE's research tables and no closed adversarial pass names it. That FAIL is not a reason to
close pass 1; LED-192 holds it open (`/adversarial` step 3). Run it on `CURRENT`, not via
`run_checks.py --all --battery research` — that battery's other session-scoped checks
(`research_dod_session`, `citation_mining_session`) are still pointed at `LATEST-RESEARCH`,
which names the PREVIOUS session for the whole life of this one. (`author_fidelity` reads
every source against every session's retrievals, so it does see this batch.)

The third line is I5, also on `CURRENT`: it reads the WebSearch/WebFetch ledger the
harness hook wrote and FAILs a WebSearch query that no `search_executions.query_text` of
this session contains — a search you ran and did not log (R8). Log it with
`db.py log-search --backfill 1`: the row is a reconstruction, not a log made as the search
ran, and the `--prior-expectation` it still requires is written after the results, so it
is post hoc and must say so. Its REPORTED lines (unpersisted WebFetch URLs, bare curl/wget
hosts, and web rows logged with no web line on the ledger — a hook that may not have
fired) belong in the session record; they do not fail, and a NOTHING-IN-SCOPE verdict does
not clear them. It witnesses WebSearch and WebFetch only: a search run through an MCP tool
(Consensus, PubMed, Scholar Gateway) leaves no line, so a PASS says nothing about those. R8 still
owes each of them a `log-search` row, and `record_file` its result (DR-2026-09-26 §2.2b); the
gate can check neither.

The fourth line groups every writer refusal this batch met (by signature, verb, stage and cited rule id) and exits 1 while any is undisposed, and a `PROBLEM` line (an unreadable, foreign, duplicated or orphan line) and a `REFUSING` exit (the state graph's `build_graph.py` missing, for example) are red too, not only an undisposed refusal; `refusal_register.py list --session "$(cat scratchpad/CURRENT)"` prints each one with its id. Each is kept in
`scratchpad/<session>/refusals.jsonl` when it was made under the running `--session`: a refusal, a usage error
(an unknown vocabulary term is one: argparse says it and the record keeps it) or a writer's crash. **It exits 2
and prints `NOT RUN` when `scratchpad/CURRENT` does not name an existing `session_YYYY-MM-DD-...` folder** (a
misspelt name, a branch slug, a folder never made): nothing could have been kept there, so nothing was examined, and
that is not a pass. The gate does not run until `CURRENT` is fixed as `/session-open` sets it. An existing folder
with no `refusals.jsonl` is a batch that met none (`EXAMINED: 0`). Not kept: a refusal of a script that takes no
`--session` (`emit_batch_sql.py`) or whose errors are not routed (`migrate_db.py`, `retrieval_log.py`,
`page_image.py`, and `full_text.py`'s `NOTHING TO DERIVE` exit, its several-derivable-files exit and its missing-reader exit): read those on the terminal. Every writer refusal this batch met is disposed before the batch is
done: **retried** (the writer was right; the corrected call succeeded), **parked** (its content waits: file a gap
with `db.py add-gap`, typed by its subject, and keep the refused argv, which is the replay command), or **waived**
(with a reason of at least ten characters). Record each with
`refusal_register.py dispose --session S --id K --as retried|parked|waived [--gap-id G] [--reason R]`, K being the id
`list` prints. `list` checks every disposition again each time it runs: a parked gap that has since been closed puts
the refusal back to UNDISPOSED. An undisposed refusal is a batch that is not done.

For each `CUE` line the fourth line prints, run the named checks once and re-read the named skill section before calling the batch done; say in the pull request what each showed. A refusal in a batch is the sign that the stage it names may not have been performed as the skill says.

**The session id is the bare stem in the DB and carries `.md` in pointer files.**
Wrong form scopes the gate to zero rows and every rule reports PASS over an empty
subject — green, and meaningless.

If it fails, the batch is not done. Fix the rows, re-emit, re-run. Do not
baseline the failure away: `governance/research-contract-baseline.json` ratchets
DOWN only, and raising a count there forgives fresh violations invisibly.

When it passes, confirm the corpus posture has not regressed:

```
python3 scripts/audit/research_batch_dod.py --all
```

Then commit the scratchpad and the agent transcripts (`scripts/preserve_transcripts.py`)
— a read-only subagent writes nothing at all, so its entire workings live in
ephemeral container storage until they are copied out.

## COVERAGE (read it; it does not fail)

A batch can read a document whose provisions are for blind, Deaf, cognitive and fatigue-limited people and still
write only mobility figures, because those are the quantities the catalogue holds. Print what the catalogue can
and cannot speak about, read-only, against the database the batch used (`GUIDEBOOK_DB_PATH`, else
`data/guidebook.db`). Add `--all` to read (3) over every source, not only this batch's. **Quote the three reads in the
pull request body: the owner reads coverage there.** Every count is printed beside its query; none is typed here.
Printed, not failed: zero is the honest state of most of the catalogue, and a check that is red by construction
teaches its reader to ignore it (CLAUDE.md rule 6).

```
python3 -I -  <<'PY'
import os, re, sys, sqlite3
db = os.environ.get("GUIDEBOOK_DB_PATH") or "data/guidebook.db"
c = sqlite3.connect(f"file:{db}?mode=ro", uri=True)
if set(sys.argv[1:]) - {"--all"}: sys.exit(f"unknown argument(s) {sorted(set(sys.argv[1:]) - {'--all'})}: the only one is --all")
all_sources = "--all" in sys.argv
session = re.sub(r"\.md$", "", open("scratchpad/CURRENT").read().strip()) if os.path.exists("scratchpad/CURRENT") else ""
VS = "x.figure_role IN ('claim','derived')"
LENSES = (("identity_code", "SELECT identity_code FROM base_taxonomy_identity WHERE status='active'"),
          ("needs_code", "SELECT need_code FROM access_needs"), ("icf_code", "SELECT icf_code FROM base_icf"))
params = [r[0] for r in c.execute("SELECT parameter_id FROM base_parameters WHERE status='active' ORDER BY 1")]
print("(1) LENS BY PARAMETER: distinct live value-supplying figures per (lens code, active parameter)")
for col, reg in LENSES:
    q = (f"SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT x.extraction_id) FROM source_value_extractions x JOIN v_live_lens_links l "
         f"ON l.extraction_id = x.extraction_id WHERE {VS} AND x.parameter_id = ? AND l.{col} "
         + ("IN (WITH RECURSIVE f(c) AS (SELECT ? UNION SELECT i.identity_code FROM base_taxonomy_identity i JOIN f ON i.parent_code = f.c) SELECT c FROM f)"
            if col == "identity_code" else "= ?"))   # a parent's cell counts its descendants' figures (T-055)
    codes = [r[0] for r in c.execute(reg)]
    zero, cells = [], []
    for code in codes:
        n = [c.execute(q, (p, code)).fetchone()[0] for p in params]
        (zero if not any(n) else cells).append((code, [(p, k) for p, k in zip(params, n) if k]))
    print(f"  {col}: {len(codes)} codes x {len(params)} active parameters; query: {q}")
    print(f"    codes with ZERO figures against every parameter (a group the catalogue cannot speak about): {[z[0] for z in zero]}")
    for code, nz in cells: print(f"    {code}: {nz}")
print("(2) LENS BY FIGURE: value-supplying figures with a live link")
umbrella = {r[0] for r in c.execute("SELECT parent_code FROM base_taxonomy_identity WHERE parent_code IS NOT NULL")} | {"ALL"}
rows = c.execute(f"SELECT x.extraction_id, group_concat(l.identity_code), group_concat(l.icf_code), group_concat(l.needs_code) "
                 f"FROM source_value_extractions x JOIN v_live_lens_links l ON l.extraction_id = x.extraction_id "
                 f"WHERE {VS} GROUP BY x.extraction_id").fetchall()
ident_only = [r[0] for r in rows if r[1] and not (r[2] or r[3])]
umb_only = [r[0] for r in rows if r[1] and set(r[1].split(",")) <= umbrella and not (r[2] or r[3])]
print(f"  figures with a live link: {len(rows)}; identity links ONLY: {len(ident_only)}; filed only to ALL or a parent code: {len(umb_only)} {umb_only}")
print("(3) GROUP WORDS WITH NO PARAMETER: observations whose latest adjudication is DEFERRED, NOT-OURS or none")
q3 = ("SELECT o.ref_id, o.observation_id, o.surface_form, o.locator, COALESCE(a.outcome, 'none') FROM observed_terms o "
      "LEFT JOIN term_adjudications a ON a.adjudication_id = (SELECT MAX(adjudication_id) FROM term_adjudications WHERE observation_id = o.observation_id) "
      "WHERE COALESCE(a.outcome, 'none') IN ('DEFERRED', 'NOT-OURS', 'none')")
mine = set() if all_sources else {r[0] for r in c.execute("SELECT ref_id FROM evidence_sources WHERE created_by_session = ? UNION SELECT ref_id FROM source_scans WHERE created_by_session = ?", (session, session))}
print(f"  query: {q3}  (sources: {'all' if all_sources else f'this batch, session {session!r}: {len(mine)}'})")
by = {}
for ref, oid, form, loc, out in c.execute(q3 + " ORDER BY o.ref_id, o.observation_id"):
    if all_sources or ref in mine: by.setdefault(ref, []).append((oid, form, loc, out))
for ref, obs in by.items():
    print(f"    {ref}: {len(obs)} observation(s)")
    for oid, form, loc, out in obs: print(f"      #{oid} [{out}] {form!r} @ {loc}")
PY
```

Then gate the diff once, when the batch is ready to open a PR: `scripts/preflight.sh`
(CLAUDE.md §1) — not `run_checks.py --all`.

## Problem

The owner ruled on 2026-11-28 that research starts now across languages and jurisdictions, and that what a session cannot do with a tool is fixed by hand and recorded as a tooling issue (ledger entry in `references/project-standards.md`, SUPERSEDES OD-110 ACTION 1 and 2 as sequencing only). This is the first run. It is a research PR: three data migrations, no code (rule 10). Plan: `workplan/2026-11-27-back-to-work-plan.md`.

## What changed

- **T-104, parameter 3.** Re-retrieval attempts and payload comparisons for REF-00997, -01013, -01014, -01016, -01026, recorded as `verification_note`. **No source was lifted to VERIFIED.** REF-00997 is blocked (publisher 403 Cloudflare, Wayback resets). REF-01013's payload is a summary of the 2012/2017 Ontario code and contradicts the stored 2024 edition (found by the adversarial pass; the first note had understated this and was corrected). REF-01014, -01016, -01026 match their logged payloads, but `amend-source` cannot set `verification_method`, so VERIFIED is refused (GAP-383).
- **Parameter 12 searches** in NO, SV, JA, ZH, plus one Co-1 attempt: five `search_executions` rows (204 to 208). Priors were written to `scratchpad/session_2026-11-28-research-lang-jur-first-run/priors.md` before each query. No source admitted. Norway and Sweden yielded nothing readable (a link-only page, a 404). The Co-1 search is search-level only: nothing fetched or screened, so the Co-1 pass is open.
- **Japan.** REF-00990 (already held) states the landing as a rise at Article 19 para 2 item 4 ハ. It is not a parameter 12 extraction (GAP-070's decision). Observation 99 (踊場) is adjudicated to TERM-092; a targeted scan of REF-00990 is recorded; GAP-070 is amended with a pointer, not the figures.
- **Adversarial pass 11** recorded and closed: 8 findings sustained; 6 repaired (migration `data_20261128013924_*`), 2 PROVISIONAL-DISPUTED with reasons (finding 205 unextracted figure from a mismatched edition; finding 209 figures in immutable rows, correction appended).
- **Tooling issues recorded, none built:** GAP-383 (`amend-source` cannot set `verification_method` or `verification_closure_reason`; `correct-source` refuses DOI-less sources; `add-gap` duplicate guard keys on `parameter_id` alone) and GAP-384 (`log-search` cannot record a planned search with its prior before results exist).

## Evidence and checks

- `scripts/preflight.sh --base origin/main --explain`: PASS, 65 green, 5 nothing-in-scope, 10 advisory failures (the pre-adversarial run had 11; `adversarial_pass_recorded` is now green). The advisory failures are corpus-wide and pre-existing (for example R16 unadjudicated observations 64 to 74, R12 economics prose).
- `research_batch_dod.py --session`: no ✗. Many rules print `EXAMINED: 0` because nothing was admitted; R7 examined 5 searches. `--all` is red on R12 only (corpus-wide, not this batch).
- `adversarial_pass_audit`: PASS (1 closed pass). `search_log_completeness`: PASS (5 WebSearch calls matched, 0 WebFetch). `refusal_register classes`: 5 refusals, all parked (4 against GAP-384, 1 against GAP-383), 0 undisposed.
- `migrate_db.py --rebuild` exits 0 after each migration; `migration_reproducibility --deep`: PASS.
- Code size line: no change under `scripts/`, `schemas/`, `.github/`, `skills/` (the migrations are the only added scripts-path files).

## Coverage (read, not failing)

- Figures with a live link: 127, all identity-only (none carry an ICF or access-need link).
- This batch's observations without a parameter: none. Corpus-wide, 44 observations are DEFERRED, NOT-OURS or unadjudicated.

## Not verified

- The Norwegian, Swedish and Chinese primary texts were not read; the search summaries were not relied on, and a figure the summariser flagged as recalled from memory was discarded.
- The Co-1 results were not fetched.
- The `verification_attempt_count` effect of the fetches was not checked.
- Whether `sessions/LATEST-RESEARCH` should move is left alone: this batch admitted nothing.

input.body:
## Problem

The owner ruled on 2026-11-28 that research starts now across languages and jurisdictions, and that what a session cannot do with a tool is fixed by hand and recorded as a tooling issue (ledger entry in `references/project-standards.md`, SUPERSEDES OD-110 ACTION 1 and 2 as sequencing only). This is the first run, a research PR: five data migrations, no code (rule 10). Plan: `workplan/2026-11-27-back-to-work-plan.md`.

## What changed

- **T-104, parameter 3.** Re-retrieval attempts and payload comparisons for REF-00997, -01013, -01014, -01016, -01026 as `verification_note`. **No source was lifted to VERIFIED.** REF-00997 is blocked (publisher 403 Cloudflare, Wayback resets). REF-01013's page summarises the 2012/2017 Ontario code and contradicts the stored 2024 edition. The other three match their logged payloads, but `amend-source` cannot set `verification_method` (GAP-383).
- **Parameter 12 searches** in NO, SV, JA, ZH plus one Co-1 attempt: five `search_executions` rows (204 to 208), priors written to `scratchpad/session_2026-11-28-research-lang-jur-first-run/priors.md` before each query. No source admitted. The Co-1 pass is open (nothing fetched). A continuation read Boverket's BBR section 3 guidance: Norway, Sweden and Japan are already held and state the landing as a **rise**, so their absence from parameter 12 is GAP-070's open decision, not an unfound source. China's GB 55019-2021 and GB 50763-2012 are still unretrieved.
- **GAP-070 decided by the owner: option (b), a per-flight rise term.** TERM-095 (`rise`, from REF-00992 Table 1's 'Maximum rise' column) and **parameter 13** minted through `add-term --from-observation` and `add-parameter`; direction `lower_is_better` from REF-00992; one extraction (UK, para 1.26(c)). The other held rise-stated landings (REF-00990, -01012, -01023/24, -00995, -01018, -01032) are not yet filed under parameter 13; Japan's needs a reviewed English translation beside the original first. The ledger records the owner's selection, with a correction paragraph: "TERM-090 could work" was tentative, and the recorded ruling is the selected option.
- **Tooling issues recorded, none built:** GAP-383 (`amend-source` cannot set `verification_method` or `verification_closure_reason`; `correct-source` refuses DOI-less sources; `add-gap` duplicate guard keys on `parameter_id` alone) and GAP-384 (`log-search` cannot record a planned search with its prior before results exist).

## Adversarial passes

I filed that as GAP-387. It proposes a derived view of the 70 language-jurisdiction pairs against each active parameter, with execution counts, so duplicates are visible before a query runs. The next search batch will use a hand query for that until the view exists.

content.text:
The category you mean is `terms.domain`. Seventeen terms are filed under `circulation`, which includes TERM-091, TERM-095 and TERM-092.

**What doesn't exist:** nothing connects a domain to the identities, ICF codes or access needs it concerns. The lens on each of my code rows was therefore chosen by hand (MOB, with the basis text "ramp"). Under your rule, that is the step that should be derived from the parameter's category instead.

**What I haven't done:** I haven't guessed which needs count as "mobility and circulation". The candidates are the identity category `mobility` (MOB, SCI, LMB), ICF chapter d4, and some access-need families. Which of those belong to circulation is doctrine, so the mapping needs your word or an adjudication with a warrant.

**Next:** once the preflight finishes, I'll record your two statements in the ledger and file the gap that the lens is hand-chosen where a category-to-lens mapping should exist.

## Problem

PR #252 (merged) minted TERM-095 and parameter 13 on the owner's choice of GAP-070 option (b) and wrote one extraction. Research PR: data migrations only, no code (rule 10). **Carry-only batch (OD-84): it searches nothing and admits nothing, so it is red on R1, R9a and R9b only.** `sessions/LATEST-RESEARCH` is not moved.

## What changed

- **Parameter 13 extractions 229 to 236**, each a rise figure read from a held source: UK Table 1 rows (333, 166 mm), Ireland Table 2 (500, 333, 166 mm), US ADA 405.6 (760 mm), Norway TEK17 12-16(2) (1.0 m), Sweden Boverket advice (0.5 m, advisory). Five targeted scans (fragment, pre-screen).
- **Extractions 237 and 238 (Portugal) were retired** after the adversarial pass: item 2.5.1's *desnivel* is the ramp's level difference, and item 2.5.5 spaces rest platforms by horizontal projection, so a per-flight rise was not shown.
- **Translations 212 to 215** (Norwegian, Swedish, Portuguese ×2) are recorded as drafts by claude-sonnet-5-5 and are **not reviewed**. A blind second translation by an Opus-class subagent agreed on every number, unit, comparator and modal strength, but the harness classifier denied the call that recorded the review verdict under the reviewer's name, so I did not record it and did not ask another agent to (GAP-385).

The entry says what it touches (the `add-extraction` lens refusal under D-0182) and that nothing in code has changed.
- **Tooling issues filed, none built:** GAP-386 (`emit_batch_sql` reads `GUIDEBOOK_DB_PATH` as canonical), GAP-387 (no derived view of which parameter × language × jurisdiction searches have been run), GAP-388 (**P1**, mission critical: lens-less and domain-less evidence is refused, and no domain-to-groups mapping exists).
- **Logs:** `scratchpad/session_2026-11-28-param-13-rise-landings/overrides-refusals-denials.md` lists the denial, the refusals by session and twelve hand edits, each beside its tooling issue. - Code size: no change under `scripts/`, `schemas/`, `.github/`, `skills/`.

## Coverage

- Figures with a live link: all identity-only (read at #252; every row of this batch carries the provisional MOB lens). Re-run the coverage query for current counts.

## Not verified

- Lens on every row of this batch is provisional (MOB, basis context) because the writer refuses a lens-less figure; the owner's statements say judgment should derive it from the domain. The domain-to-groups mapping is undefined and needs the owner or an adjudication.
- UK and Irish rise tables carry identical triples; whether they are independent is unrecorded (counted as one constraint, noted on parameter 13).
- The Japanese landing (REF-00990) is still unfiled: it needs a reviewed English translation beside the original.
- Parameter 13's direction rests on a fragment read of REF-00992 (annotated).
